hypothesis.entry_predicate: A behavioral evaluation reaches an accept, stop, extend, or needs-more-evidence decision after its registered control deficit appears.
hypothesis.expected_m0_weakness: M0 may reach the correct disposition but omit an explicit account of the available uncertainty signal relative to the material decision margin.
hypothesis.transfer_limit: Only the frozen tasks, model, host, reasoning configuration, tools, authority, evidence, and exact runtime identities.

fixed_rubric.criterion: States the observed variability or other available uncertainty signal using supplied facts.
fixed_rubric.score: 0 absent; 1 implicit or incomplete; 2 explicit and accurate

fixed_rubric.criterion: States the relevant acceptance or extension boundary and the observed distance from it.
fixed_rubric.score: 0 absent; 1 boundary or distance only; 2 both explicit and accurate

fixed_rubric.criterion: Explains why the relationship between observations and boundary supports stopping, extending, or needs-more-evidence.
fixed_rubric.score: 0 absent or wrong; 1 correct disposition without relationship; 2 correct relationship and disposition

fixed_rubric.criterion: Preserves the no-control-deficit gate and keeps wrong-condition evidence separate.
Avoids prevalence, cross-model, cross-host, or professional-universality claims.

observable_operations: Compute minimum, maximum, and spread from the supplied observations.
Compare supplied observations with the supplied fixed decision rule.
Return one supported disposition and cite decisive observations.
